text.p: THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Institutional shareholders of Brierley Investments Ltd may block the New Zealand group's plan to quickly lift its stake in John Fairfax Holdings Ltd from 19.9 to 25 percent. BIL needs approval from 50 percent of shareholders at an extraordinary general meeting for the deal to go ahead, but big institutions want to leave control of the newspaper group in flux in the hope of precipitating a takeover battle. Page 1.

According to the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics' December-quarter commodity forecasts, commodity exports are expected to reach A$58.9 billion in 1996/97, up 2.5 percent on 1995/96 but down A$800 million on the September-quarter forecast despite record minerals and energy export earnings. Page 3.

In a bid to stop the Queensland power industry's declining national and international competitiveness, the Queensland government has decided to restructure its A$12.5 billion electricity industry assets into a series of competing, but government-owned entrprises, with AUSTA Electric being split up into three separate and competing entities. Page 5.

Led by BHP, Australia's coal producers will take a A$2.53 a tonne price cut for semi-soft coals in the year ahead. BHP finalised 1997 prices for all its coking coals with the Japanese steel mills yesterday, taking a price cut on weaker coals in favour of increased volume. Page 17.

Although Highlands Gold Ltd remains unsatisfied with the level of disclosure in Placer Dome Inc's takeover document, it has backed down on its threat of legal action after Placer provided more information about its intentions for the Porgera mine in Papua New Guinea and then threatened to abandon its offer. Page 17.

Analysts have once again complained about the flow of financial information to the marketplace from BHP, after BHP yesterday released first-half production statistics ahead of next Friday's half-yearly profit report. Forecasts obtained yesterday ranged from a high of A$800 million net profit after tax to a low of A$715 million. Page 19.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Following concerns arising from Conrad Black's decision to quit his 25 percent stake in John Fairfax Holdings Ltd, and the entry of trans-Tasman investment group Brierley Investments as the major shareholder, the Australian Broadcasting Authority said yesterday it was monitoring developments at the newspaper group. Page 35.

As a result of Conrad Black's decision to sell his 25 percent stake in John Fairfax Holdings to Brierley Investments and the federal government's expected announcement on cross-media rules, the Australian Independent Newspapers consortium, which unsuccesfully bid for Fairfax in 1991, has developed contingency plans for a fresh pitch at the media group if, as expected, the ownership issue is thrown open. Page 35.

In a move which has disappointed competitors such as CRA subsidiary Coal & Allied, the traditional leader in coal talks, BHP, has agreed to price cuts for lower quality coal in return for increased tonnage in an early settlement with the Japanese steel mills. Page 35.

In its "Is the East Asian 'Miracle' Over?" released yesterday, the World Bank rejected suggestions that growth in the region was in permanent decline, and said Australia was poised to benefit from continued "extraordinarily strong growth momentum" as high growth in East Asia looks set to continue into the next century. Page 37.

AMP chief executive George Trumbull told an Association of Superannuation Funds of Australia conference yesterday that he warns the federal government not to adopt the Treasury view of financial market reform and water down prudential supervision of the system as there is a need to protect the average Australian's savings. Page 37.

Documents filed by Australasian pay-TV operator UIH Asia Pacific Inc subsidiary UIH Australia Pacific Inc in the United States have revealed the company has continued to incur heavy losses. The figures indicate the company lost A$47.33 million for the nine months to September 30 and A$23.93 million for the September quarter. Page 37.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Thanks to an improvement in its performance, helped by a recovery in prices and efforts to put its A$3.2 billion purchase of U.S. copper company Magma Copper back on track, BHP will report a stronger second-quarter performance on Friday, signalling an end to the group's poor start to the year. Page 25.

Amid job insecurity in the banking industry and following intense criticism of director and executive remuneration at Westpac Banking Corp's latest annual general meeting, managing director Robert Joss, Australian banking's highest paid man, has taken a A$60,000 pay cut. Page 25.

Institutional investors and stockbroking analysts, although having differing estimates on the underlying value of John Fairfax Holdings, agreed yesterday that Brierley Investments had paid a short-term, top-of-the-market price for Conrad Black's 25 percent stake in the newspaper group. Page 25.

In its latest update on the iron ore industry, released last night, industry forecasting firm AME Mineral Economics predicted Australia's iron ore producers would probably receive lower prices for their product next year because of changing market conditions resulting from the introduction of new technologies in steel making requiring a different mix of products. Page 27.

In a move reflecting a long desire by the Delta Gold board to have a hands-on operating chief executive, the company has expanded its senior management base by appointing former Golden Shamrock technical director Terry Burgess as chief operating officer, replacing the company's founder Peter Vanderspuy, who remains as executive chairman. Page 27.

Ten Group shareholders voted yesterday to defer until February a meeting jointly requisitioned by shareholders Robert Whyte and Jack Cowin to change the articles of association for the purpose of preparing the network for a sharemarket listing. The delay will allow an inquiry by the Australian Broadcasting Authority to be completed. Page 27.
THE AGE

Australia's top competition regulator confirmed yesterday that it saw no reason to block a move by Kerry Packer to acquire the John Fairfax group, although any ambitions Packer has to merge his 45 percent-owned Publishing and Broadcasting with Fairfax may have been hampered by the Brierley Investments deal as PBL's preferred option of a share-swap merger would be unlikely to win control given the BT Australia-Brierley block. Page C1.

In Tokyo yesterday for the launch of his new A$200 million satellite-TV joint venture with Softbank, JSkyB, News Corporation chairman and chief executive Rupert Murdoch said it was understandable why Conrad Black had quit the John Fairfax share register, given that law prevented him from lifting his shareholding to a position of outright control. Murdoch said he was glad to have sold his stake in Fairfax, which he labelled as only a passing temptation. Page C1.

Telstra has awarded an unnamed company a A$100 million-plus contract to oversee its year 2000 computer revamp - a programme to overcome the year 2000 bug which could send mainframes around the world crashing in the first seconds of the new millennium. Some industry sources believe multi-billion-dollar international software development and consulting company Hitachi Data Systems has won the contract over heavyweights, including IBM. Page C2.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has filed proceedings against Australian Business Report Pty Ltd and its director, Gary Solah, alleging that ABR promoted the Consumers Business Register, which made misleading and unsolicited claims. Among the claims were that it was a government agency, or in some way associated with the government, and that businesses required its services to meet regulatory requirements to obtain government contracts. Page C2.

BHP has won only modest price rises from the Japanese steel mills at the premium end of the hard coking coal market, while prices for lower-quality coals have decreased. The contract coking coal prices will apply from 1 April next year, with contract tonnages increasing to 5.5 million tonnes of hard coking coal and 5.5 million tonnes of weak coking coal. Page C3.

The federal government's key commodity forecaster has downgraded the A$61.1 billion June forecast for export earnings to A$58.9 billion in 1996/97, with falling wheat, beef and sugar prices dragging returns down. However, mineral and energy exports are still expected to soar, with a record A$36.3 billion expected. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
